instructions: Separate 12 large leaves from the head of lettuce, rinse them and pat them dry. Stack them on a plate.
Mince half the onion and dice half the bell pepper into small pieces.
In a small bowl, stir together the garlic powder, cumin, chili powder, paprika, oregano and salt.
Heat the oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add the turkey and break it up with a spoon. Cook for 6 minutes, until there's no pink left and some pieces are browned.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook for 3 minutes, until they're soft.
Add the spice mix and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.

Add the tomato sauce and 1/2 cup water and scrape up anything stuck to the pan. Bring it to a simmer, turn the heat to low, cover and cook for 12 minutes. If it still looks watery, uncover it for the last 3 minutes. You're cooking the turkey to 165°F, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? It's done when there's no pink anywhere.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Spoon the turkey into the lettuce leaves and serve with the salsa.
method_notes: Skinnytaste (4.84 from 50 ratings) is the lead: brown lean turkey, add the spices, then simmer it with onion, bell pepper and tomato sauce. Its 20-minute covered simmer is cut to 12 here, with a tablespoon of oil to brown the turkey and the spices stirred in hot first. Cooking Classy (5 from 19 ratings) agrees on the method but uses canned tomatoes and a 5 minute simmer. Cheese and sour cream are left off to keep it dairy-free.
